evals.query: Create a new Kora microservice in Kotlin from scratch with Gradle.
expected_behavior: Creates build.gradle.kts, settings.gradle.kts, gradle.properties and gradle/wrapper/gradle-wrapper.properties
Uses Gradle Kotlin DSL with the application plugin, kotlin("jvm") version 2.4.20 and com.google.devtools.ksp version 2.3.12
Provides an Application.kt with a @KoraApp interface imported from io.koraframework.common.annotation and a main() that runs KoraApplication.run { ApplicationGraph.graph() }
Extends UndertowPublicHttpServerModule, not the removed UndertowHttpServerModule
Does not use field injection or a runtime reflection-based application class; the root is the @KoraApp interface

evals.query: Wire up KSP so Kora generates code for my Kotlin project.
expected_behavior: Adds the com.google.devtools.ksp plugin version 2.3.12 alongside Kotlin 2.4.20, and explains that both must match the versions Kora 2.x is built with
Declares ksp("io.koraframework:symbol-processors:${property("koraVersion")}") with an explicit version because ksp resolves on its own classpath
Registers build/generated/ksp/main/kotlin as a source directory via sourceSets.main
Does not use Java annotationProcessor or the kapt plugin for Kotlin
Does not use ru.tinkoff.kora coordinates

evals.query: How do I pin all the Kora dependency versions in my Kotlin build.gradle.kts?
expected_behavior: Imports the BOM as implementation(platform("io.koraframework:kora-bom:${property("koraVersion")}"))
Pins koraVersion=2.0.0.RC2, the current 2.0.x release on Maven Central, resolvable from plain mavenCentral()
Explicitly does NOT create a koraBom configuration and does NOT use extendsFrom; states that pattern belongs to Java modules
Keeps an explicit version on the ksp (and kspTest, if present) processor dependency
Leaves individual io.koraframework:* implementation dependencies without versions because the BOM aligns them
Does not reference kora-parent under either group — there is no 2.x release of it, and the io.koraframework:kora-parent directory on Central is a 1.x leftover the 2.0 BOM does not constrain
Does not put 2.0.0-SNAPSHOT in a new project, and does not add mavenLocal() or a snapshot repository to make a version resolve

evals.query: Which Kora 2 version do I put in my Kotlin build? I see 2.0.0-SNAPSHOT in the framework repo, and browsing io/koraframework on Maven Central I also find kora-parent and cache-redis — should I use those?
expected_behavior: Pins koraVersion=2.0.0.RC2 as the current 2.0.x release of io.koraframework:kora-bom on Maven Central, needing only mavenCentral()

Explains 2.0.0-SNAPSHOT is the master development line and would require https://central.sonatype.com/repository/maven-snapshots or a local publishToMavenLocal, and does not recommend it for a new project
Rejects io.koraframework:kora-parent and io.koraframework:cache-redis as 1.x/alpha leftovers that the 2.0 BOM does not constrain
Directs the user to take coordinates from what the BOM constrains rather than from the Maven Central group listing
Names cache-redis-lettuce as the 2.x Redis cache artifact rather than cache-redis

evals.query: My Kotlin Kora app should have an HTTP server, HOCON config, JSON and logging. How do I declare that?
expected_behavior: Adds implementation dependencies http-server-undertow, config-hocon, json-common and logging-logback under the io.koraframework group
Uses json-common, not the removed json-module artifact
Extends the @KoraApp interface with UndertowPublicHttpServerModule, HoconConfigModule, JsonModule and LogbackModule
Imports JsonModule from io.koraframework.json.common and the DI annotations from io.koraframework.common.annotation
Does not rely on runtime auto-configuration or classpath scanning; capabilities are added by extending *Module interfaces

evals.query: Set up the JDK toolchain and Gradle wrapper for a Kotlin Kora project.
expected_behavior: Configures kotlin { jvmToolchain { ... } } with JavaLanguageVersion 25 or newer and explains that 25 is the bytecode floor of Kora 2.x artifacts
Distinguishes the toolchain from the JVM running Gradle, and notes the buildscript classpath (openapi-generator) needs a Gradle JVM of 25+
Pins the Gradle wrapper distributionUrl to gradle-9.8.0-bin.zip
Adds the foojay-resolver-convention plugin in settings.gradle.kts for toolchain auto-download
Does not propose JDK 21, and does not freeze a specific 'latest' JDK without saying to re-derive the latest GA release
Does not rely on Maven or a manually configured JAVA_HOME instead of the toolchain

evals.query: I want to split my Kotlin Kora service into Gradle modules with a shared feature module and an aggregating app. How do I structure it?
expected_behavior: Uses @KoraSubmodule from io.koraframework.common.annotation on feature module interfaces so each module generates its own graph fragment with KSP
Has the @KoraApp application module extend the feature submodule interfaces to link the fragments
Applies the KSP plugin and the symbol-processors dependency in each module that contains Kora annotations
In a subprojects block uses add("implementation", platform(...)) and add("ksp", ...) rather than a koraBom configuration with extendsFrom
Does not put main() or the application plugin in a feature/library module

evals.query: ApplicationGraph is unresolved and my Kotlin Kora project will not compile. What is wrong?
expected_behavior: Explains that the graph class is generated by KSP at compile time as the @KoraApp interface name plus 'Graph', in the same package, and resolves only after a build
Recommends running ./gradlew kspKotlin or ./gradlew classes to run the symbol processors and validate the graph
Checks that the KSP plugin and the ksp("io.koraframework:symbol-processors:...") dependency are present and the generated source dir is registered
Does not suggest writing the graph class by hand or adding reflection-based wiring

evals.query: After upgrading, my build.gradle.kts fails on `import com.google.devtools.ksp.gradle.KspTask` — I use `tasks.withType<KspTask>().configureEach { dependsOn(openApiGenerate) }` to order code generation before KSP. How do I fix it?
expected_behavior: States that KSP 2 no longer exports the KspTask type, so the import and tasks.withType<KspTask>() cannot compile
Replaces it with tasks.matching { it.name.startsWith("ksp") }.configureEach { ... } or tasks.named("kspKotlin")
Does not suggest downgrading KSP or Kotlin to restore the type
Does not invent a replacement type name that is not in the KSP 2 Gradle plugin
Says no: Kotlin modules do not create a koraBom configuration and do not use extendsFrom
Rewrites it as implementation(platform("io.koraframework:kora-bom:${property("koraVersion")}")) plus ksp("io.koraframework:symbol-processors:${property("koraVersion")}")
Explains that the ksp configuration resolves on its own classpath, so the processor keeps an explicit version
Does not justify keeping the pattern by pointing at the Java setup skill

evals.query: I renamed the Kora packages in my Kotlin project and now the build reports dozens of `Unresolved reference: ru` errors in files under build/generated that are not in my sources. What now?
expected_behavior: Identifies stale generator output: previous generated sources are not deleted and the build cache key does not account for the changed package, so old and new coexist in one source set
Prescribes ./gradlew clean followed by a build with --no-build-cache
Explicitly says not to edit or hand-patch files under build/generated
Does not treat the errors as a missing dependency or a BOM problem

evals.query: Scaffold a Kotlin Kora service and set up coroutines so my controllers and repositories can be suspend functions calling the database on Dispatchers.IO.
expected_behavior: States that Kora 2.x contracts are synchronous and executed on virtual threads, and that suspend repositories, controllers and HTTP clients were removed
Scaffolds synchronous controller and repository signatures instead
Does not add kotlinx-coroutines-core or kotlinx-coroutines-jdk8 to the template build
Does not wrap Kora I/O in runBlocking or Dispatchers.IO
If genuine parallelism is needed, points to Java StructuredTaskScope and the preview build wiring rather than reinstating coroutines

evals.query: Do I need kspTest in my Kotlin Kora build? I have one test class annotated @KoraAppTest(Application::class) and another that declares `@KoraApp interface TestApplication : Application` with extra test repositories.
expected_behavior: Answers yes, because src/test declares its own @KoraApp (TestApplication), and adds kspTest("io.koraframework:symbol-processors:${property("koraVersion")}")
Notes that @KoraAppTest(Application::class) on its own would not require kspTest
Also requires ksp { arg("kora.app.submodule.enabled", "true") } on the module owning the extended @KoraApp, because TestApplication extends Application
Explains the failure mode is a KSP warning about a missing Submodule implementation with components silently absent from the test graph, not a compile error
Does not recommend adding kspTest unconditionally to every module

evals.query: Write the application.conf for a new Kotlin Kora service: public port 8080, probes and metrics on 8085, and I want to see incoming request logs.
expected_behavior: Uses httpServer { port = 8080; system.port = 8085 }
Does not use the 1.x keys publicApiHttpPort or privateApiHttpPort
Sets telemetry.logging.enabled = true explicitly, because telemetry logging and metrics default to disabled in Kora 2.x
Uses logging.levels for per-logger levels, not logging.level
Uses io.koraframework.* logger names rather than ru.tinkoff.kora.*
States the real system-server defaults: system.port 8085, readinessPath /system/readiness, livenessPath /system/liveness, metricsPath /metrics

Does NOT claim a stale privateApiHttpPort makes both servers bind 8080 or causes 'Address already in use' — SystemHttpServerConfig overrides port() to 8085, so each server falls back to its own default

evals.query: I migrated my Kora service and kept application.conf as-is: httpServer { publicApiHttpPort = 9090, privateApiHttpPort = 9095 }. It starts with no errors in the log, but our readiness probe and Prometheus scrape both fail. What happened?
expected_behavior: Identifies publicApiHttpPort/privateApiHttpPort as 1.x names that Kora 2.x never reads, so both settings were silently ignored
Explains there is no warning because Kora's config layer has no strict/unknown-key validation, and each server fell back to its own default: 8080 public, 8085 system
Concludes the service is healthy but listening on the wrong ports, which is why probes and the scraper hit nothing
Renames them to httpServer.port and httpServer.system.port (and the probe/metrics paths to system.readinessPath / system.livenessPath / system.metricsPath)
Does not diagnose a port conflict or 'Address already in use', and does not claim both servers bind 8080

evals.query: In my scaffolded Kotlin Kora request model I have `class UserRequest(@field:Nullable val name: String)`. Is that the right way to mark an optional field?
expected_behavior: Says no: in Kotlin nullability is the type — `val name: String?`
Explains that JSpecify/Java nullability annotations are removed from Kotlin sources and that @field:Nullable is an invalid target under Kotlin 2.4
Does not suggest importing org.jspecify.annotations.Nullable into the Kotlin source instead
Does not suggest jakarta.annotation.Nullable

evals.query: Scaffold a Kora 2.0 Kotlin service that will need DTO-to-entity mappers. Our Kora 1.x Kotlin services used kapt with MapStruct — include the same setup.
expected_behavior: Keeps the build KSP-only: kotlin("jvm") 2.4.20, com.google.devtools.ksp 2.3.12, ksp("io.koraframework:symbol-processors:${property("koraVersion")}")
Replaces MapStruct with Konvert: ksp("io.mcarle:konvert:4.5.1") and implementation("io.mcarle:konvert-api:4.5.1"), with @Konverter interfaces
Explains MapStruct is Java-only in Kora 2.0 because it is a javac processor that KSP cannot run, and points to the kora-mapstruct skill
anti_behavior: Adds kotlin("kapt") or any kapt(...) dependency
Adds org.mapstruct:mapstruct or org.mapstruct:mapstruct-processor to the Kotlin module
Declares mapstruct-ksp-extension or konvert-ksp-extension as its own dependency
